skill.description: Guide Chakra UI v2 to v3 migrations through package updates, codemods, providers, color mode, component rewrites, theming, and Next.js integration.

No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, data exfiltration, or unrelated execution in SKILL.md.

content.user_title: Migrate Chakra UI Projects from v2 to v3
content.value_statement: Chakra UI v3 introduces breaking changes across dependencies, components, providers, and themes. This skill guides inspection, codemod review, manual rewrites, and validation in an ordered workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guide inspection of package versions, framework choices, lockfiles, provider setup, and existing v2 patterns.
Provide dependency replacement guidance and Chakra codemod commands with a dry-run review step.
Explain provider setup, semantic color tokens, and Next.js App Router and Pages Router placement.
Map common prop renames and illustrate compound component rewrites for dialogs, checkboxes, progress indicators, accordions, and fields.
Introduce createSystem, token value wrappers, recipes, slot recipes, and theme type generation.
Provide TypeScript, lint, build, interaction, visual regression, and leftover import validation checks.
limitations: The package contains instructional Markdown, not a bundled migration engine or executable codemod.
The documented workflow requires Node.js 20 or later and access to external packages for CLI operations.
Complex custom components and large themes require manual review beyond the introductory examples.
Some API examples may need correction; verify hook exports and compound component names against the installed package versions.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a React application
use_cases.description: Inspect dependencies, review a codemod dry run, and update common v2 props and component patterns before validation.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Next.js provider
use_cases.description: Review provider placement, color mode integration, and client boundaries when upgrading an App Router or Pages Router project.

use_cases.title: Plan a design system migration
use_cases.description: Map existing theme tokens and component styles to createSystem, recipes, slot recipes, and type generation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect migration readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use chakra-ui-migrate to inspect my project for a v2 to v3 upgrade. Identify versions, framework, package manager, and likely changes without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the current project state.

prompt_templates.title: Review the codemod plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the Chakra UI upgrade using my existing package manager. Explain dependency changes and the codemod dry run before requesting approval to execute commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare controlled dependency and codemod changes.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate selected components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these v2 components for v3 migration: [components]. Propose prop and compound structure changes, verify installed APIs, and identify interaction tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: update a limited component group.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a full application upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a staged Chakra UI v3 migration for this Next.js application and custom theme. Cover providers, color mode, recipes, typegen, validation, and manual review boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate application and theme changes.

output_examples.input: Review migration readiness for a Chakra UI v2 application.
output: Inspect the installed Chakra version, framework, Node version, and lockfile before selecting commands.
Review related dependency usage before removing packages that Chakra UI v3 no longer requires.
Preview codemod changes before applying them, then inspect provider, theme, and component updates.
Complete type checks, linting, builds, interaction tests, and visual review.

output_examples.input: Explain how to migrate a v2 modal and its styling.
output: Replace Modal usage with the Dialog compound structure and review its open-state callback.
Map the backdrop, positioner, content, title, body, footer, and close control to the appropriate Dialog parts.
Review renamed style props and verify the exact API against the installed v3 package.
Test opening, closing, focus behavior, and appearance in both color modes.

output_examples.input: Outline the migration of a custom v2 theme.
output: Replace extendTheme setup with createSystem and wrap custom token values in the v3 token structure.
Translate single-component styles into recipes and multipart styles into slot recipes.
Run theme type generation after updating custom tokens and recipes.
Review complex theme behavior separately and compare representative pages for visual regressions.

best_practices: Inspect installed versions and framework conventions before selecting migration commands or copying examples.
Review the codemod dry run and keep codemod changes separate from manual edits.
Validate exact package APIs, types, builds, interactions, and light and dark appearances after each migration stage.
anti_patterns: Apply codemod changes without reviewing the dry run or resulting diff.
Remove shared dependencies without checking whether unrelated application code still uses them.
Copy illustrative snippets without verifying package exports, event signatures, or compound component names.

faq.question: Which Chakra UI versions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on migrating Chakra UI v2 projects to v3, including package, provider, component, and theme changes.

faq.question: Does the skill perform migrations by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for an assistant and documents external CLI tools that can change project files and dependencies.

faq.question: Which runtime does the workflow require?
faq.answer: The skill specifies Node.js 20 or later for Chakra UI v3. Confirm compatibility with your selected package versions.

faq.question: Does the codemod handle every change?
faq.answer: No. The guide requires dry-run review and manual checks, especially for custom components, event handlers, and complex themes.

faq.question: Does it cover Next.js applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses App Router and Pages Router providers, client boundaries, color mode, and Link and Image composition.

faq.question: Can I copy every example unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Verify current package APIs, especially color mode hooks and compound component names, then run type, build, interaction, and visual checks.
